issues.legal_issue: An appeal from an arbitrator’s award under the governing compensation scheme is heard as an appellate proceeding, not as an application to set aside the award.
material_facts: The compensation dispute had been referred to an arbitrator under a statutory scheme that provided an appeal to the High Court.
The Government appealed the arbitrator’s award to the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court heard the appeal as an appellate court, rather than as a court deciding an application to set aside an award.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 19(1)(f) of the Defence of India Act, 1939, the High Court acts as an appellate court when hearing an appeal from an arbitrator’s award; it does not act as a court hearing an application to set aside the award. The Court relied on Collector of Varanasi v. Gauri Shankar Misra.

predicates.statutory_compensation_award_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal to the High Court from an arbitrator’s award of compensation.

issues.definition: When the proceeding is an appeal to the High Court from an arbitrator’s compensation award, the High Court exercises appellate jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A party’s failure to produce relevant account books in its possession may support an adverse inference against its compensation claims.
material_facts: The claimant sought compensation for damage to a building and for water pipes.
The claimant had maintained accounts relating to construction and repairs but did not produce them.
The claimant did not produce accounts that could have shown the length of pipes used.
The High Court reduced the amounts awarded for the building damage and the pipes, and the Supreme Court upheld those reductions.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to disallow the major part of the claims for building damage and water pipes because the relevant account books were not produced.
issues.legal_principle: When a person fails to produce account books in that person’s possession, an adverse inference may be drawn. The Court relied on Seth Maganmal Since Deceased v. Darbarilal Chowdhry, AIR 1928 PC 39.

predicates.compensation_award_appeal: The proceeding challenges an appellate court’s reduction of compensation amounts awarded by an arbitrator.
predicates.relevant_accounts_held: The claimant maintained or possessed accounts relevant to the claimed damage or materials.
predicates.relevant_accounts_not_produced: The claimant did not produce those relevant accounts as evidence.

issues.definition: If a compensation-award appeal concerns reduced claims and the claimant possessed but did not produce relevant accounts, the reduction of claims supported by those accounts is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Interest is not recoverable as a matter of right, and interest cannot be awarded as damages.
material_facts: The claimant sought interest as part of the compensation claim.
The arbitrator awarded interest in an amount slightly greater than the amount claimed.
The High Court disallowed the interest, and the Supreme Court upheld that decision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court rightly disallowed the interest awarded by the arbitrator.
issues.legal_principle: A claim for interest is not a matter of right, and interest by way of damages cannot be awarded.

predicates.compensation_award_appeal: The proceeding challenges an appellate court’s decision concerning interest included in an arbitrator’s compensation award.
predicates.interest_claimed_as_damages: The claimant seeks interest as damages in the compensation proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns interest claimed as damages in a compensation proceeding, interest as damages is not awarded.
